extractions.quote: Stiff-person syndrome (SPS) also called stiff-man syndrome, is an immune-mediated CNS disorder characterized by progressive rigidity of the trunk and proximal limb muscles, associated with intermittent superimposed spasms and heightened sensitivity to external stimuli. The spasms are often triggered by emotions, such fear and unexpected tactile, auditory or emotional stimulation1. In most cases, SPS is associated with high levels of serum and cerebrospinal fluid autoantibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD-65), the rate-limiting enzyme for the synthesis of a major inhibitory neurotransmitter, gamma-amino-butyric acid (GABA). ... Serum anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase autoantibodies (antiGAD-Abs) were abnormally elevated at 44 U/mL (normal values are below 1 U/L). ... Electromyography (EMG) of lower limbs revealed continuous motor unit activity at rest.
